verse.text: brahmārpaṇaṁ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam | brahmaiva tena gantavyaṁ brahmakarmasamādhinā ||

howto.text: Before the first bite: put a little water in the palm, look at the food, and say the verse once. Then eat as if the meal is being offered into a fire — slowly, without hurry. The feeling to find: gratitude with heat. Nothing extra; the verse does the whole work.

verse.text: asmadrūpa samāviṣṭaḥ svātmanātma nivāraṇe | śivaḥ karotu nijayā namaḥ śaktyā tatātmane ||

howto.text: Say it silently as the food arrives. The 'obstacle' can be anything — the craving, the guilt, the person you're eating with. Name it, then let the verse dissolve it.

verse.text: ātmīyaviṣayabhogairindriyadevyaḥ sadā hṛdambhoje | abhipūjayanti yaṃ taṃ cinmayamānandabhairavaṃ vande

howto.text: At the first bite, feel the heart-lotus (just behind the centre of the chest) as the altar and the flavour as the flower landing on it. Three bites only — overdoing it kills the taste. The feeling: gratitude with heat. The sense is honoured as a goddess, not supervised as a thief.

verse.text: prapañcottīrṇarūpāya namaste viśvamūrtaye | sadādivyaprakāśāya svātmane'nantaśaktaye

howto.text: On waking: recite as its placement asks. The verse's own act is namaḥ — homage, phrase by phrase, one round.

verse.text: deho devālayaḥ proktaḥ svātmā devaḥ sanātanaḥ | tyajedajñānanirmālyaṃ so'haṃ bhāvena pūjayet

howto.text: The verse's own method: cast off the sweepings of ignorance and hold so'ham as the worship — the bhāva is the practice, not a formula.

verse.text: jāgratasvapnasuṣuptyādyā dhārayaṃśca nijāḥ kalāḥ | svecchayā bhāsi naṭavan niṣkalo'si ca tattvataḥ

howto.text: On waking: say it once. The verse itself performs the recognition — the states named as his rays, nothing else to do.

verse.text: tvatprabodhāt prabodho'sya tvannidrāto layo'sya yat | atastvadātmakaṃ sarvaṃ viśva sadasadātmakam

howto.text: Last line of the day. Lie down and take one awake minute: you are about to do what he does at night. Don't stay awake doing this — fall asleep inside the thought.

verse.text: anāgatāyāṃ nidrāyām praṇaṣṭe bāhyagocare | sāvasthā manasā gamyā parā devī prakāśate

howto.text: At lights-out, on your back, one hand on the belly. Wait for the outer field to fade — sounds go dull, images slow. Then instead of following sleep passively, send the mind as an arrow to the heart-centre, once. Then release. The Goddess-feel is a hum or warmth behind the chest; if images swarm you have grasped — release and let the hum carry. Single-shot: no repetitions.

verse.text: aśeṣaviṣayāśūnyaśrīsamāśleṣasusthitaḥ / śayīyam iva śītāṅghrikuśeśayayuge kadā

howto.text: In bed. Say it once, then let the image of the two cool feet form under the mind's eye — no details needed, just the coolness. The feeling to find: the fever of the day dropping. If the mind races, return to the coolness, not the words.

verse.text: viṣamastho 'pi svastho 'pi rudann api hasann api / gambhīro 'pi vicitto 'pi bhaveyaṃ bhaktitaḥ prabho

howto.text: Use it when waiting has turned into agitation — a queue, a delay, a message that won't come. Say it once inwardly. Don't wait for composure: the very mess is the place where devotion can be.

verse.text: anubhūyāsamīśāna pratikarma kṣaṇāt kṣaṇam / bhavatpūjāmṛtāpānamadāsvādamahāmudam

howto.text: At any transition or pause: say it once, then take one breath as if that breath were the nectar. Don't manufacture joy — notice the small lift that a pause already gives. Three pauses, three sips, and the waiting has changed colour.

verse.text: svātmani viśvagaye tvayi nāthe tena na saṃsṛtibhītikathāsti | satsv api durdharaduḥkhavimohatrāsavidhāyiṣu karmagaṇeṣu

howto.text: When negative, say it and let the concession stand: yes, this is hard; and the fear of it is separate from the pain itself. The verse splits them.

verse.text: evameva parā pūjā sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā | aikyabuddhayā tu sarveśe mano deve niyojayet

howto.text: Before opening the laptop: one line, then begin. The test for aikyabuddhi: the boundary of your skin thins. If it sharpens, you're thinking oneness, not yoking it — drop to the breath and restart. Each task is one yoke; re-hitch as often as needed.

verse.text: śivo bhūtvā yajeteti bhakto bhūtveti kathyate / tvam eva hi vapuḥ sāraṃ bhaktair advayaśodhitam

howto.text: At the desk, when work feels like a distraction from practice: say it and reclassify. The spreadsheet, the email, the conversation — that is the worship.

verse.text: kurute bhairavapūjāmanaladalasthā'bhimānakusumairyā | nityamahaṅkṛtirūpāṃ vande tāṃ śāmbhavīmambām

howto.text: When the ego flares mid-task — pride, irritation at the colleague, hunger for recognition: see it as a flower, pick it, place it at the heart's fire. Three flowers are enough.

verse.text: tvatsvarūpe jṛmbhamāṇe tvaṃ cāhaṃ cākhilaṃ jagat | jāte tasya tirodhāne na tvaṃ nāhaṃ na vai jagat

howto.text: Use it at the overwhelm point — too much to do, the self tightening. Say it and feel the day as one exhale of a larger form. The overwhelm thins because the 'me' carrying it is part of the expansion, not its owner. Then return to the next small task.

verse.text: svātmaprabhāṃ vidhāya vāgdevīṃ viṣayakusumakḷptārcaḥ | prathamonmeṣaṃ gurum atha vanditvā hṛdayam āviśya

howto.text: Before a difficult conversation, a speech, a message you'll regret: one breath, hand on the throat. Make the speech a light — not a blade. Offering the sense-flowers means: don't weaponise what you've seen and heard. Then speak from the heart-entered place, not the throat.

verse.text: śabdaḥ kaścana yo mukhādudayate mantraḥ sa lokottaraḥ saṃsthānaṃ sukhaduḥkhajanmavapuṣo yatkāpi mudraiva sā | prāṇasya svarasena yatpravahaṇaṃ yogaḥ sa evādbhutaḥ śāktaṃ dhāma paraṃ mamānubhavataḥ kinnāma na bhrājate

howto.text: Use it after you've said something — ordinary, even stupid. That was mantra. The recognition flips the whole day: the meeting, the small talk, the complaint — all of it is mantra, mudrā, yoga, shining.

verse.text: alaṃ bhedānukathayā tvadbhaktirasacarvaṇāt | sarvamekamidaṃ śāntamiti vaktuṃ ca lajjate

howto.text: Use it when an argument about views has you mid-sentence — or when you're about to explain your practice to someone who doesn't need it. Stop. The shyness is the right register.

verse.text: nirmalasya kutaḥ snānaṃ vastraṃ viśvodarasya ca | nirlepasya kuto gandho ramyasyābharaṇaṃ kutaḥ

howto.text: In the shower: name each item as you use it — water for the stainless, towel for the world-bellied, scent for the unanointed. The mismatch is the smile.

verse.text: antarullasadacchācchabhaktipīyūṣapoṣitam / bhavatpūjopayogāya śarīram idam astu me

howto.text: Dressed, before leaving the bathroom: say it once and feel the freshly washed body as anointed rather than merely clean. The day ahead is the pūjā; the body is the instrument.

verse.text: udayāvabhāsacarvaṇalīlāṃ viśvasya yā karotyaniśam | ānandabhairavīṃ tāṃ vimarśarūpāmahaṃ vande

howto.text: At dawn, as placed: the verse's own act is vande — praise of the ceaseless play she keeps performing.

verse.text: svayaṃ prakāśamānasya kuto nīrājanaṃ vibhoḥ | vedavācāmavedyasya kutaḥ stotraṃ vidhīyate

howto.text: At the bathroom mirror, hand raised with the light: you are the lamp-bearer, and the face that brightens is the audience. Hum, don't articulate — you have just honoured the Vedavācāmavedya.

verse.text: pūrṇasya dakṣiṇā kutra nityatṛptasya tarpaṇam | visarjanaṃ vyāpakasyā'pratyakṣasya kṣamāpaṇam

howto.text: Use it at the end of the bath as the day's closing already: one bow, weight the last word — pardon. The feeling is the end of accounting: no tally of errors, no debt. Guilt arrives, is named as one of the litany's items, and dissolves with the god it expected to offend.

verse.text: brūṣe nottamāṅga paśyasi na māmetādṛśaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vijñaptiṃ bahudhā kṛtāṃ na śṛṇuṣe nāyāsi manmānase | saṃsārārṇavagartamadhyapatitaṃ prāyeṇa nālambase vākcakṣuḥśravaṇāṅghriṇādirahitaṃ tvāmāha satyaṃ śrutiḥ

howto.text: Use it when you've spoken and nobody heard — human or divine. Say the whole complaint with feeling; the scripture-clause at the end is the punchline that dissolves it.

verse.text: māyīyakālaniyatirāgādyāhāratarpitāḥ / caranti sukhino nātha bhaktimanto jagattaṭe

howto.text: Before or after a meal, when desire is loudest: name it as the course — māyā, time, fate, desire — and eat it. The hunger is the menu.

verse.text: saṃsāro 'sti na tattvatas tanubhṛtāṃ bandhasya vārtaiva kā bandho yasya na jātu tasya vitathā muktasya muktikriyā | mithyāmohakṛd eṣa rajjubhujagacchāyāpiśācabhramo mā kiṃcit tyaja mā gṛhāṇa vihara svastho yathāvasthitaḥ

howto.text: In the queue, the delay, the silence: say the last line — 'live healthy, staying as you are.' The restlessness wants to grab something or drop something; the verse forbids both.

verse.text: na kiñcid eva lokānāṃ bhavadāvaraṇaṃ prati yat kiṃ cid eva bhūtānāṃ

howto.text: Use it in any crowd — the queue, the train, the meeting. Run the census once: two classes. Then check which one is noticing the census.

verse.text: ānando 'tra na vittamadhyamadavan naivāṅganāsaṅgavat dīpārkendukṛtaprabhāprakaravan naiva prakāśodayaḥ | harṣaḥ saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr bhārāvatāropamaḥ sarvādvaitapadasya vismṛtanidheḥ prāptiḥ prakāśodayaḥ

howto.text: In bed, say it and feel the day's weight as the literal bhāra being lowered. Bliss here is not an event but an unloading.

verse.text: yātastvatsahavāsato bahutaraḥ kālo vatāsmin kṣaṇe kiṃ kiṃ vā na kṛtaṃ tvayā varagurūpāsānimittena me | vāraṃ vāramahaṃ punarnirupamāṃ divyaṃ bhuvaṃ prāsuvatkāyastvāṃ kila vismarāmi yadataḥ stheyaṃ na bhūyastvayā

howto.text: When ill and feeling forgotten: say the whole verse as the complaint it is — 'what has not been done by you for me?' — and let the last line be the request.

verse.text: bhavatpādāmbujarajorājirañjitamūrdhajaḥ / apārarabhasārabdhanartanaḥ syām ahaṃ kadā

howto.text: From the sickbed, say it as a question — kadā, when — without demanding the answer today. Picture only the dust on the hair; the dance can wait.

verse.text: antardehe mayā nityaṃ tvamātmā ca gaveṣitaḥ | na dṛṣṭastvaṃ nacaivātmā yacca dṛṣṭaṃ tvameva tat

howto.text: When pain or weakness is present: look at it once — the ache as an object — and name it 'seen: you.' Not as denial of pain but as address change.

verse.text: śṛṇu devī! paraṁ guhyaṁ rahasyaṁ paramādbhutam | sarva-pāpa-praśamanaṁ sarva-duḥkha-nivāraṇam || prāyaścitteṣu sarveṣu tīvreṣv api vimocanam | sarva-cchidrāpa-haraṇaṁ sarvārti-vinivārakam || samayolaṅghane ghore japādeva vimocanam | bhoga-mokṣha-pradaṁ devī! sarva-siddhi-phalapradam ||

howto.text: Recite it at the beginning and end of any ritual — the hymn's own instruction (yāgārambhe ca yāgānte). Also daily (nitya), on occasion (naimitika), when you want something (kāmya), for yourself or for someone else. Counting effects per the hymn: one hundred recitations purify even great sinners; fifty, inadvertent sins; twenty-five, minor sins — and a single recitation (of this hymn or of the Aghora japa) removes wrongs done by body, speech or mind, whether through inattention or knowingly.

verse.text: vidhihīne pramāde ca japtavyaṁ sarva-karmasu | nātaḥ parataro mantro nātaḥ paratarā stutiḥ || nātaḥ paratarā kācit samyak-pratyaṅgirā priye | iyaṁ samaya-vidyānāṁ rāja-rājeśvarī-śvari || paramāpyāyanaṁ devi bhairavasya prakīrtitam | prīṇanaṁ sarva-devānāṁ sarva-saubhāgya-vardhanam ||

howto.text: Full practice in the tradition: dhyāna of Svacchanda (crystal-white upward face, yellow east, blue south, pomegranate-red north, moon-white west — the twelve-verse meditation), then this hymn, then the Gāyatrī — oṁ bahurupāya vidmahe, koṭarākṣāya dhīmahi, tanno 'ghoraḥ pracodayāt, three times — then the mūla mantra. In this book's simpler use: one round of these three verses at the close of any difficult day; the line to remember is 'no mantra greater than this'.

verse.text: oṁ bahurupāya vidmahe, koṭarākṣāya dhīmahi | tanno 'ghoraḥ pracodayāt

howto.text: The recitation order per the viniyoga: dhyāna → hymn → this gāyatrī three times → mūla mantra. Three rounds, seed-voice. 'Pracodayāt' is the only request in the entire sequence — everything before it was arrangement.

verse.text: oṁ namaḥ śivāya

howto.text: Say it aloud or mentally: let naḥ open, maḥ hold, śi release, vā hide, ya return. The Name does the work — no count needed, pick it up any hour.
